newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus central bank chief held in graft probe.
newsitem.headline: Belarus central bank chief held in graft probe.

text.p: The head of Belarus' central bank has been sacked and arrested in connection with a corruption investigation, President Alexander Lukashenko's office said on Tuesday.
A statement read on the former Soviet republic's national radio said Tamara Vinnikova had been detained by police after being accused of "damages to the state of major proportions".
A source in the public prosecutor's office said Vinnikova, appointed by Lukashenko last February, was alleged to have extended illegal credits to a bank and a large firm.

Lukashenko told the inaugural session on Monday of the new upper chamber of parliament that Vinnikova, 46, was one of three candidates to head the central bank, indicating he was thinking of removing her.
He mentioned nothing of impending criminal proceedings but said commercial banks had spoken against her.
"I cannot help but take account of the opinion of the leaders of banks of such stature," he told the chamber.
Acting Prime Minister Sergei Ling had predicted her dismissal saying that although a specialist "she perhaps lacks experience, broad vision and administrative capabilities".
Vinnikova replaced Stanislav Bogdankevich, a reformer effectively forced from office by Lukashenko to the dismay of Western financial institutions seeking liberalisation and change.
She had earlier been head of the large Belarus Bank, which merged with the state savings bank in August 1995 to create the largest bank in the country of 10 million.
Vinnikova had initially been an unquestioning supporter of Lukashenko's reluctant approach to market reforms when appointed but over time objected to many of his policies.
She opposed Lukashenko's decision to lower refinancing rates without consulting the central bank and the creation of a corridor to regulate the rate of the Belarussian rouble.
